pain_points.title: Fund Control Gaps in Group Operations

items.title: Personal QR Code Collection
items.desc: Stores and project teams accept payments via personal WeChat or Alipay accounts, bypassing group accounts so headquarters cannot track inflows in real time.
items.consequences: Off-book fund loops, reconciliation pain, distorted operating data.

items.title: Third-Party Account Diversion
items.desc: Business receipts flow into third-party platforms or personal accounts outside group control, creating off-book pools and weakening centralized fund scheduling.
items.consequences: Fragmented funds, compliance exposure, decisions without reliable data.

items.title: Fragmented Payment Channels
items.desc: Each legal entity connects to payment providers independently with different rates and settlement cycles, making reconciliation error-prone and costly.
items.consequences: Unreliable reporting, high maintenance, complex integrations.

items.title: Off-Book Fund Pools
items.desc: Some revenue never reaches governed accounts or moves through informal channels, so the group cannot see true operating and fund positions.
items.consequences: Weak internal controls, costly audits, low fund transparency.

architecture.title: Enterprise Governance Architecture
architecture.lead: Centralized governance at headquarters. Independent operations at each legal entity.
architecture.lead_en: Governance stops at the Organization level, preserving each legal entity's operational independence.
architecture.reinforcing: Governance centralizes management without centralizing operations.
architecture.not_org_chart: This diagram illustrates governance relationships only — not actual org counts or hierarchy depth.
architecture.example_footnote: Example: a diversified group may map Enterprise to group headquarters, Organization to a business-unit legal entity, and Merchant to a store or project operator (Example only — not any specific company or partnership).

items.title: Enterprise Governance
items.desc: Headquarters creates and manages legal entities centrally. Governance stops at the Organization level — it does not replace day-to-day operations or authorization.

items.title: Unified Collection
items.desc: Group-wide acquiring strategy and channel coordination, with each legal entity signing and operating under its own entity while funds stay transparent and controllable.

items.title: Smart Settlement
items.desc: Licensed split-payment APIs automate clearing, reducing manual transit and supporting multi-entity, multi-scenario settlement.

items.title: Full-chain Audit
items.desc: Governance actions, authorization changes, and fund flows are fully traceable for headquarters oversight and compliance audit.

governance_model.title: Governance Model
governance_model.intro: FilixPay separates governance responsibilities from day-to-day business operations, allowing headquarters to maintain visibility and control without replacing each legal entity's operational authority.

rules.title: Core Business Rules
items: Enterprise governs at the group level (creating and managing Organizations). It does not directly own, control, or suspend Merchants — authorization stays within each Organization.
The group may set unified acquiring policies; each Organization signs and operates under its legal entity.
Customer payments flow into supervised accounts — external collection channels and personal QR codes are prohibited.
Licensed split APIs automate clearing and reduce manual fund transit risk.
Cross-organization fund movements require group approval before execution.

scenario_0.title: Enterprise Setup
scenario_0.process: Create Example Enterprise → Create Example Organization → Invite Organization Owner → Create Example Merchant 01 → Start Operations
scenario_0.value: Stand up group governance quickly — independent entity operations with headquarters-wide visibility.

scenario_1.title: Scenario 1: Subsidiary Sells Group Products
scenario_1.process: Customer pays → Group account (unified collection) → Group recognizes revenue → System allocates subsidiary commission
scenario_1.value: Protects group fund sovereignty with automated settlement.

scenario_2.title: Scenario 2: Joint Sale Split
scenario_2.process: Single order includes group products and subsidiary services → Split API at payment → Funds route directly to multiple accounts by ratio
scenario_2.value: No second transfer — compliant and timely.

scenario_3.title: Scenario 3: Inter-Entity Internal Transfer
scenario_3.process: Organization initiates request → Group approves → Funds move within supervised group account → Target Organization
scenario_3.value: Fully traceable internal collaboration without funds leaving the governed perimeter.

compliance.title: Compliance & Risk Control
items: Unified collection and supervised account pooling — no personal QR codes or off-book pools
Licensed institution split APIs — the group does not hold customer balances in transit
Acquiring, contract, and invoicing entities stay aligned with automated checks
Full operation trails, multi-level approval for rule changes, auditable governance actions
Cross-border splits connect to trade-service FX filing with transaction evidence retained

performance.hero_desc: A stepped k6 load test on the production OpenAPI create-order endpoint, validating stability and latency under concurrent write workloads.
performance.metrics_subtitle: Stepped load from 1 to 50 concurrent users with 0% error rate throughout.
performance.recommended_limit: Recommended production rate limit: ~100 TPS (stable capacity × 70%).

capacity.title: Daily Order Capacity Estimate
capacity.subtitle: Based on an 8-hour business day with a 4-hour peak window.
capacity.intro: Using the stable throughput from this load test, we estimate how many orders the create-order API can handle in a typical business day.
capacity.assumption_hours: Business assumption: 8 active hours per day for order creation.
capacity.assumption_peak: Peak assumption: 4 peak hours at the recommended limit of 100 TPS.
capacity.assumption_off_peak: Off-peak assumption: the other 4 hours are estimated at 30% of peak, i.e. 30 TPS; a flat 100 TPS for all 8 hours is also provided as a full-rate reference.
capacity.highlight_daily_desc: 4 peak hours at 100 TPS + 4 off-peak hours at {offPeak} TPS
capacity.highlight_daily_flat_desc: All 8 hours at 100 TPS (off-peak also at 100 TPS)
capacity.highlight_peak_desc: At the recommended limit of 100 TPS

rows.daily_full: 8 business hours (full load-test throughput, theoretical max)

capacity.disclaimer: These figures reflect create-order API capacity on a single tested deployment. Payment, refund, query, and other APIs are excluded. Production planning should also consider peak factors, redundancy, and monitoring.

methodology.item1: Endpoint: POST /openapi/v1/orders with Client Credentials authentication
methodology.item2: Scenario: minimal order payload with required fields only; no payment channel calls
methodology.item3: Tool: Grafana k6 stepped load up to 50 VUs for 19 minutes 30 seconds
methodology.item4: Data: test orders prefixed with LOADTEST- for identification and cleanup

performance.evidence_subtitle: k6 summary output and system resource monitoring captured during the load test.
performance.screenshot_summary_caption: Figure 1: k6 summary — 165,229 orders created at 141 TPS, P95 353 ms, P99 404 ms, 0% errors.
performance.screenshot_50vu_caption: Figure 2: 50 VU peak — Java and MySQL are the main CPU consumers; overall CPU ~61%, service remained available.
performance.screenshot_20vu_caption: Figure 3: 20 VU stage — load increases progressively with application and database under shared pressure.
performance.conclusion_body: The FilixPay OpenAPI create-order endpoint remained stable at 50 concurrent users with 100% success rate and 404 ms P99 latency, providing a credible baseline for capacity planning and integration expectations.
performance.cta_title: Need higher concurrency or private benchmarking?
performance.cta_desc: Contact us for tailored performance assessment and deployment options.

identity.title: Identity & Auth
identity.hero_title: Enterprise Identity: Building a Financial-Grade Security Foundation with Keycloak
identity.hero_desc: In payment systems, identity authentication is not only the first door of user experience but also the core defense line for fund security and compliant operations. We adopt Keycloak - an open-source Identity and Access Management (IAM) platform led by Red Hat - as a unified identity authentication engine, providing financial-grade security, global compliance support, and capacity for tens of millions of users for your payment business.
identity.why_keycloak_title: ✅ Why Keycloak? — Verified by Top Global Institutions
identity.why_keycloak_desc: Keycloak has been deeply adopted by numerous industries with high security requirements, including finance, government, telecommunications, and cloud computing:

cases.name: Hitachi
cases.desc: Built an authorization server for Japanese banks that meets Financial-grade API (FAPI) standards, passing 700+ consistency tests to meet the most stringent open banking compliance requirements.

cases.name: Austrian Federal Computing Centre (BRZ)
cases.desc: As a technology partner of the Austrian government, it supports unified authentication for 2 million+ users and 130+ public services, operating stably for many years.

cases.name: Infosys
cases.desc: Built an identity platform for a large Japanese pharmaceutical group, managing over 2 million users and supporting 4000+ pharmacists logging in safely daily in 750+ pharmacies.

cases.name: VMware (Broadcom)
cases.desc: Deeply integrated Keycloak into its Telco Cloud Operations platform to achieve automated management of users, roles, and permissions.

identity.cases_conclusion: These cases prove: Keycloak can not only handle high concurrency and large-scale user pressure but also meet the compliance thresholds of highly regulated industries such as finance and government.
identity.features_title: 🔐 Security Capabilities Tailored for Payment Scenarios
identity.feature_1_desc: Full implementation of OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0; native support for FAPI (Financial-grade API) security specifications to meet PSD2 and open banking compliance; support for PKCE, MTLS, JWT signature verification, and other advanced security mechanisms.
identity.feature_2_desc: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): SMS, TOTP, WebAuthn (FIDO2); Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and fine-grained permission policies; session management: automatic timeout, forced logout, and device binding.
identity.feature_3_desc: GDPR Ready: Data minimization, consent management, data export/deletion; PCI DSS Friendly: No contact with cardholder data (PAN), serves only as an authentication layer, reducing compliance scope; compatible with multi-level protection scheme (MLPS) requirements.
identity.feature_4_desc: Supports cluster deployment, database sharding, and cache optimization; proven in multiple national platforms to handle millions of daily active users; private deployment ensures data sovereignty and network isolation.
identity.integration_title: 🛠️ Seamlessly Integrate with Your Payment System
identity.integration_desc: Keycloak provides standardized interfaces for easy integration with:
identity.integration_footer: Also supports federation with existing identity sources like LDAP, Active Directory, and social accounts for a smooth migration without burden.
identity.choice_title: 💡 Our Choice: Open Source + Enterprise-Grade Protection
identity.choice_desc: Keycloak is a Red Hat-supported open-source project, giving you:
identity.choice_item_1: Cost advantage with zero licensing fees
identity.choice_item_2: Technical ecosystem with active community and comprehensive documentation
identity.choice_item_3: Enterprise SLA support options with Red Hat Single Sign-On (Commercial version)
identity.cta_quote: "We chose Keycloak not just because it's free, but because it's been verified by global financial and government institutions—it's an identity engine truly capable of carrying the security of payment systems."
identity.cta_desc: Experience now: Our payment platform has a built-in Keycloak authentication system, supporting rapid connection to your existing IAM system, helping you achieve a perfect balance between security and efficiency.
